D005-D010_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling like something’s really off for the past couple of months. At first, I thought it was just stress—work’s been hectic, and I’ve been trying to launch this big redesign for a client. But then I started seeing things… like shadows moving in the corner of my apartment, or figures standing across the street who vanish when I look directly. Last week, I swear I saw a man outside my window at night, just staring, but when I turned the light on, no one was there.

I keep thinking the world is… ending, somehow. Not in a metaphorical way—I mean, infrastructure failing, everything collapsing soon. It feels inevitable. I’ve stopped opening my design files because what’s the point if nothing will matter in a few weeks?

There was this stretch a few weeks ago where I hardly slept, but I was hyper-focused—redesigning mockups at 3 a.m., sending dozens of emails, feeling like I could fix everything instantly. My husband said I was talking too fast, like I was on something, but it didn’t feel bad at the time. Now I’m not sure if that energy was real or just part of the breakdown. The visions started before that phase, and they haven’t really gone away, even though the high-energy rush faded after a couple of weeks.

    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia

D005-D010_h002.question:

D005-D010_h007.question:

D005-D010_h021.question:

I look around at my clients, the courthouse, even my own apartment, and it all seems fake, like a set for a play that already closed.

I’ve been sleeping maybe two hours a night, but I’m not tired. I’ve drafted five business plans for absurd startups—like a restaurant for pets that mimics human therapy sessions. I know it’s ridiculous now, but at the time, it felt brilliant.

It’s not constant—some days are clearer. But the voices? They’ve been here the whole time, steady as rain. I can’t tell if the wild ideas are mine or theirs. And I don’t know if this started before the racing thoughts or after. It’s all blurred.
